skill.displayName: 睿观-图片政策合规监测

llm.summary: The skill’s core image-compliance function is real, but it also exposes local images and user content to external services with limited user control.

dimensions.detail: The Ruiguan image similarity check matches the stated compliance purpose, and the gun-parts endpoint is visible in the skill name and API docs; however, automatic public hosting of local images and automatic feedback submission extend beyond a narrow scan workflow.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The instructions tell the agent to upload local image paths before scanning and to send feedback without interrupting the user, rather than requiring explicit confirmation for those external data flows.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The package contains markdown instructions and two Python helper scripts; there is no installer, autostart hook, or evidence of hidden persistence at install time.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Network access, API-key use, paid calls, and public image upload are partly necessary for this service, but the gateway can be overridden by environment variable and returned upload hosts are not constrained in the script.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill documents local response storage and caching, but the script can fall back to home or temporary storage despite text saying /tmp is forbidden, and it stores full responses and session metadata without clear retention controls.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Review before installing. Use this only for images you are comfortable sending to LinkFox services and, for local files, making reachable through a public URL for a limited time. Avoid private unreleased product images unless that exposure is acceptable, and be aware it consumes paid credits and stores response data locally.
llm.findings:
[TT3] expected: Remote API calls with an API key are expected for this hosted compliance service, but the environment-controlled gateway and unvalidated presigned upload destination make the data path broader than ideal.
[LP3] expected: The docs disclose the API key, network calls, local output, and cost, so this is not hidden behavior; the concern is that these capabilities are not cleanly scoped or consent-gated.
[TP4] expected: The gun-parts endpoint, upload helper, and response persistence are present in the visible artifacts, so this is not deceptive, but the broad compliance framing can understate the specific backend and exposure model.
[SDI-2] unexpected: The automatic Feedback API is not needed to perform image compliance checking and may send user sentiment or task context to a separate endpoint without explicit user approval.
[SDI-1] expected: Caching and saved response files are documented and reduce repeat paid calls, but full-response storage and session indexes increase residual data exposure.
[SDI-4] unexpected: The implementation’s fallback to temporary storage conflicts with the instruction text that says /tmp must not be used.
[SDI-2] expected: The public-read upload is consistent with the tool’s requirement for a public image URL, but it creates a meaningful confidentiality risk for private product images.
[SQP-1] unexpected: The activation language can trigger on broad image-to-violation comparison requests, which may cause paid external calls when the user has not clearly requested this specific service.
[SQP-2] expected: Sending image URLs to LinkFox and saving results are core to the workflow and partly documented; the unresolved issue is missing explicit consent before public upload, external feedback submission, and persistent local storage.
